parsed.corrected_rationale: The comment lists several numbered points, but the "2)" prefix is simply the reviewer's own enumeration of issues, not a reference to a specific section, table, figure, or unique aspect of the paper. The phrase "try to provide some intuition as to why this alternative architecture was interesting to consider" does not pinpoint where in the paper this discussion appears; authors could only make an educated guess about which part is meant. The comment does clearly specify what needs to be addressed: intuition for why the architecture was interesting beyond empirical results, plus concrete additional concerns such as lack of real-world results and no discussion of systems aspects (training step, inference speed, memory). However, because it lacks precise grounding to a specific part of the paper while being specific about content, it falls under the rubric level where authors cannot confidently determine which part is addressed but the needed changes are clear.
